library_notes: Mathlib `Nat.digits_length_le_iff` ((b.digits n).length ≤ k ↔ n < b^k) and `Nat.lt_digits_length_iff` (k < (b.digits n).length ↔ b^k ≤ n) turn the two power bounds into the Nat.digits endpoint; `Nat.length_digits` / `Nat.digits_len` give (digits b n).length = Nat.log b n + 1. These are library retrieval and are flagged, not forbidden.

Direct kernel evaluation is not available: `decide` / `norm_num` refuse exponents above the elaborator threshold (256) and hit maxRecDepth on 2^565248 < 10^170157 (checked 2026-09-22 in the common environment), so the sharp bounds need a structured proof (block decomposition with Nat.pow_lt_pow_left / pow_mul / pow_add, as the released chain does); the coarse bound in witness_min.lean uses the same tools at one block.
Nat.pow_lt_pow_left, Nat.pow_le_pow_right, pow_mul, pow_add, mul_pow, Nat.mul_lt_mul_of_lt_of_lt, Nat.lt_of_mul_lt_mul_left are the fair shared ingredients.
